# Authentic legacy kernel fixtures

These synthetic fixtures are generated by the actual standalone `memcore` 1.9.2
revision `eba0c48617e8820831bfd22f91d269c6d70f409f`. No user database or personal
content is included. The committed manifests and data were generated from that
revision; each artifact also carries the revision and real schema version.

The independent generator uses the old kernel's public `upsert`,
`import_snapshot_batch`, and companion outbox APIs. It then seeds ordinary
historical auxiliary rows through SQLite. It never changes `user_version` to
pretend that a newer database is old. The independent manifest pins that exact
Git revision with default features disabled; it does not use the current kernel
or require a machine-specific sibling checkout.

The coordinating agent runs it under the repository's approved host Cargo gate,
with the same serialized build resources as other validation. From the ZeroClaw
checkout, the command is:

```bash
scripts/dev/cargo-local.sh run --locked --manifest-path crates/zeroclaw-memory/tests/fixtures/legacy-kernel/Cargo.toml --bin generate-legacy-kernel-fixture -- /absolute/path/to/new-output-directory
```

The output directory must not exist. Inspect the generated schema version and
data before copying `memory-schema-v38.json` and `companion-schema-v38.json` into
`crates/zeroclaw-memory/src/portable_migration/`, and `memory-v38.json` and
`companion-v38.json` into this fixture directory. The emitted `.db` files are validation scratch, not committed
fixtures. Keep the generator's lockfile with the fixture for reproducibility.

The manifests preserve exact SQLite object SQL and complete column shapes.
Production old-pin FTS uses `simple`; a hand-edited `unicode61` schema is not an
admitted alternative. The old kernel explicitly tolerates an unavailable vec0
projection, so absence of the entire known vector projection is supported.
Opaque FTS and vec0 shadow data is omitted from fixture rows: canonical virtual
tables recreate it from logical rows, while the manifests still verify every
shadow object's definition.

Fixture restoration creates tables and unique indexes before inserting rows,
uses deferred foreign-key checks for the transaction, restores sequence high
watermarks after rows, and installs persistent triggers last. This avoids
inventing guard functions or disabling protective triggers on a live store.

The migration's semantic verification excludes the internal SQLite `rowid` of
`memories` and `hard_state`: their stable identities are respectively `id` and
`(namespace, key)`. The admitted old schema has no foreign-key reference to those
internal rowids. Every other ordinary auxiliary rowid and every admitted
AUTOINCREMENT high watermark is preserved. Kernel migration/profile/role stamps
are generated by the new kernel; all ordinary hard-state columns and historical
host receipts remain in the verification projection. Only the new migration
receipt's exact UUID key is excluded from its own digest.

The generic fixture contains four memories, a logical vector, a revision-zero
archived row with empty lifecycle values, an unarchived superseded row, and a
different agent's record. Ordinary history includes an orphan access event and
an empty BLOB that must remain distinct from NULL. The companion fixture has
four capture memories and five outbox events. Its pending, in-flight and
acknowledged states include a genuinely stale acknowledged revision and a
conflict resolved by the old public `resolve_outbox_conflict(LocalWins)` API:
the quarantined original and pending `::local-wins` successor retain separate
identities, revisions, digests and timestamps. The body event ID stays unchanged.

The committed artifact SHA-256 values are pinned in the fixture test. Data
timestamps are produced by the real old writer, so regeneration requires
reviewing and updating those data hashes; schema hashes remain reproducible.

## Filesystem and refusal boundary

The converter and its filesystem tests support Unix only. A caller must stop
source writes and exclusively control the trusted destination directory until
completion. Its owner must match the private staging directory's owner; group
or other-user write permission is refused. Staging is `0700`, database and
marker files are `0600`, and directory and published-file identities stay bound
to held file handles through final reopen and fsync.

The original DB, WAL, SHM and recognized sidecar file set are censused and hashed
before and after copying and again before publication. SQLite only opens a
private DB/WAL copy; original SHM read marks are never updated, and missing SHM
is not created. Only committed WAL frames enter the consistent backup. Any
observed source change aborts this offline operation.

Failed private work is cleaned up. Once publication starts, rollback removes
only files whose paths still point at the originally held DB or marker inode.
Unknown sidecars and replacement files are refused and retained; failures do
not promise to remove another writer's residue. Deterministic tests inject a
source change, foreign sidecars, and a replacement database. This checks the
observed-change boundary without claiming protection from an adversarial
same-UID process performing undetectable ABA changes between filesystem calls.
